'''''Chenopodium ficifolium''''', the '''fig-leaved goosefoot''' or '''figleaf goosefoot''', is a plant species in the family Amaranthaceae originally native to the [[Irano-Turanian Region|Irano-Turanian floristic region]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1= Nobis|first1= Agnieszka|last2= Nowak|first2= Arkadiusz|last3= Rola|first3= Kaja|title= Do invasive alien plants really threaten river bank vegetation? A case study based on plant communities typical for ''Chenopodium ficifolium''—An indicator of large river valleys|journal= PLOS ONE|volume= 13|issue= 3|article-number= e0194473|doi=10.1371/journal.pone.0194473 |pmid= 29543919|pmc= 5854390|year= 2018|bibcode= 2018PLoSO..1394473N|doi-access= free}}</ref> It is an [[archaeophyte]] weed in Europe and can now be found in temperate crop-growing regions in most of the world.<ref>{{cite book |date= 2014-09-25|title= Harrap's Wild Flowers|isbn=978-1-4081-8987-0 |last1= Harrap|first1= Simon}}</ref>
